mainEntity.name: How much does a Volkswagen Golf 1.2 or 1.4 TSI engine replacement cost?

acceptedAnswer.text: A Volkswagen Golf 1.2 TSI engine replacement typically costs £1,500-£2,800 supply-only for a rebuilt unit, with 1.4 TSI units from £1,800-£3,500. Used engines start from £600. Total fitted cost adds 8-14 hours of labour at specialist rates (£65-£85/hr) or dealer rates (£120-£180/hr).

mainEntity.name: What are the signs of timing chain failure in a Volkswagen Golf 1.2/1.4 TSI?

acceptedAnswer.text: The most common sign of timing chain stretch in the EA111 engine is a metallic rattle on cold start, lasting 1-3 seconds. As wear progresses, you may hear a continuous rattle, experience poor acceleration, rough idle, hesitation, or see the engine management light illuminate with correlation fault codes (P0016, P0341).

mainEntity.name: Is it worth replacing the engine in a Volkswagen Golf 1.2 or 1.4 TSI?

acceptedAnswer.text: This depends on your Golf's overall condition and market value. For a well-maintained Mk6 or Mk7 (worth £4,000-£10,000), a rebuilt engine at £1,500-£3,500 is viable, especially with the 12-month warranty. For an older Mk5 example worth under £3,000, a used engine or targeted repairs may be more cost-effective.

mainEntity.name: How long does a Volkswagen Golf 1.2 or 1.4 TSI engine replacement take?

acceptedAnswer.text: A Volkswagen Golf TSI engine replacement typically takes 2-3 working days for a specialist workshop, including removal of the old unit, fitting the replacement, and road testing. Main dealers may quote 3-5 days due to scheduling and OEM parts ordering.

mainEntity.name: What's the difference between the EA111 and EA211 TSI engines?

acceptedAnswer.text: The EA111 (CBZB, CAXA, CAVD) is a chain-driven engine used from 2005-2012, known for timing chain tensioner failure. The EA211 (CJZA, CJZB, CYVA) is a belt-driven engine introduced from 2012 onwards, with improved reliability but a finite timing belt service life. The EA111 1.4 TSI twincharger (CAVD) adds a supercharger for 160bhp but is the most complex and failure-prone variant.

mainEntity.name: Should I buy a used or rebuilt engine for my Volkswagen Golf 1.2 or 1.4 TSI?

acceptedAnswer.text: Used engines are cost-effective (£600-£1,400) but come with unknown service history and no warranty beyond the supplier's standard 30-90 days - risk of the same timing chain or turbo issues reoccurring. Rebuilt engines (£1,500-£3,500) include new timing components, piston rings, bearings, turbo refresh, and a 12-month unlimited-mileage warranty, offering peace of mind for long-term ownership.

historyTimeline.h2: Volkswagen Golf 1.2 TSI & 1.4 TSI - Engine History & Specs at a Glance
historyTimeline.intro: The Volkswagen Golf 1.2 TSI and 1.4 TSI engines were introduced as part of Volkswagen's TSI (Turbo Stratified Injection) family, offering efficient turbocharged petrol power across the Golf Mk5, Mk6 and Mk7 generations. The 1.4 TSI arrived first in 2005, followed by the 1.2 TSI in 2008, with a major engineering split between the earlier EA111 chain-driven units and the later EA211 belt-driven engines introduced from 2012 onwards.

milestones.description: 1.4 TSI 122bhp (CAXA) - Golf Mk5 launch, 1,390cc, DOHC 16-valve, turbocharged, timing chain
1.2 TSI 105bhp (CBZB) - Golf Mk6 launch, 1,197cc, SOHC 8-valve, turbocharged, timing chain
1.2 TSI 105bhp (CJZA) - EA211 belt-driven engine introduced, improved reliability
1.2 TSI 86bhp (CJZB/CYVA) - EA211 lower-power variant, timing belt
1.4 TSI 122bhp (CAXA) - Continued in Mk6 with updated tensioner design
1.2 TSI phased out - Replaced by 1.0 TSI in Golf Mk8

historyTimeline.closingNote: Every engine fitted to the Volkswagen Golf 1.2 TSI and 1.4 TSI is covered below, with UK rebuilt pricing and known failure points.

items.title: CBZB (2008-2012)
items.commonFailure: The CBZB is an EA111 chain-driven engine. Timing chain stretch and tensioner failure are well-documented, typically occurring from 60,000-100,000 km (37,000-62,000 miles). Cold-start rattle is the primary warning sign. Oil change intervals of 20,000 miles are too long - frequent oil changes are critical to prevent chain wear.

items.commonFailure: The CJZA is an EA211 belt-driven engine. Timing chain issues are replaced by timing belt concerns - replacement interval is typically 60,000-100,000 miles. Water pump leaks and oil consumption have also been reported.

items.title: CJZB / CYVA (2013-2020)

items.title: CAXA (2005-2014)
items.commonFailure: The CAXA is an EA111 chain-driven engine - one of the most notorious for timing chain stretch and tensioner failure. The tensioner can fail from around 50,000 km (31,000 miles), with the early CAXA-family tensioner being the common culprit before Volkswagen revised the design. Cold-start rattle, loss of power, and correlation fault codes (P0016, P0341) are classic symptoms.

items.commonFailure: The CAVD twincharger unit is complex - it suffers from the same EA111 timing chain tensioner issues, plus additional problems: supercharger clutch failure, turbocharger actuator issues, and high oil consumption. Repairs are expensive - a proper rebuild can easily exceed £4,000 in parts alone.

commonProblems.h2: Volkswagen Golf TSI Engine Problems - Repair Cost vs Replacement
commonProblems.h3: The Volkswagen Golf 1.2 TSI and 1.4 TSI engines are popular for their efficiency and performance, but they have well-documented weak points - timing chain tensioner failure on EA111 units, timing belt wear on EA211 units, and turbocharger issues. Rebuilt Golf TSI engines supplied through EnginesMarket typically include upgraded timing components, new water pump, and refreshed turbocharger hardware, plus a minimum 12-month unlimited-mileage warranty.

problems.h4: Timing Chain Tensioner Failure - Why the Volkswagen Golf 1.2/1.4 TSI EA111 Rattles
problems.affectedModels: Volkswagen Golf 1.2 TSI (CBZB) and 1.4 TSI (CAXA, CAVA, CAVD), 2005-2012
problems.rootCause: The EA111 timing chain tensioner is a known weak point. The design is poor - chains stretch and the tensioner fails, causing timing to jump. Early CAXA-family tensioners are the common culprit before Volkswagen revised the design. Symptoms include cold-start rattle, rough idle, hesitation, poor fuel economy, and power loss. If ignored, the chain can jump teeth, causing bent valves and catastrophic engine failure.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: New chain, tensioner, guides, sprockets. Requires significant engine disassembly. 8-12 hour job.
repairOptions.longevity: Viable if caught early (cold-start rattle only). Prevents catastrophic failure.

repairOptions.tier: Cylinder head rebuild (if chain has jumped)
repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Remove cylinder head, replace bent valves, new guides and seals, timing components.
repairOptions.longevity: Required if chain has jumped and valves have contacted pistons.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Supply & fit, rebuilt engine with upgraded timing components, 12-month warranty
repairOptions.longevity: Best if chain has snapped, if bore scoring is present, or if head rebuild + other work exceeds 60% of replacement cost.

problems.vehicleValueCheck: A typical Volkswagen Golf 1.2/1.4 TSI of relevant age (2005-2014) sits in the £2,000-£8,000 value band, depending on generation, mileage, and condition. For examples under £3,500, a timing chain replacement at specialist rates (£900-£1,600) is borderline but defensible. For higher-value Mk6 examples (£5,000-£8,000), a full rebuilt engine with warranty (£1,800-£3,500) is the safer long-term investment.
problems.recommendation: If you hear a cold-start rattle from your Golf 1.2/1.4 TSI, get it diagnosed immediately. A timing chain replacement caught early is far cheaper than a full engine rebuild. If the chain has already jumped or snapped, a full rebuilt engine with warranty is the only sensible option - the warranty protects you against secondary failure.
problems.cta: -> Compare rebuilt EA111 Volkswagen Golf TSI engine prices

problems.h4: Timing Belt Wear - EA211 Engine Service Requirements
problems.affectedModels: Volkswagen Golf 1.2 TSI (CJZA, CJZB, CYVA) and 1.4 TSI (EA211 variants), 2012-2020
problems.rootCause: The EA211 engine uses a timing belt, not a chain. Unlike the chain-driven EA111, the belt has a finite service life. Replacement intervals are typically 60,000-100,000 miles. If the belt fails, valves contact pistons causing catastrophic engine damage.

repairOptions.tier: Timing belt, water pump & tensioner replacement
repairOptions.whatItInvolves: New timing belt, tensioner, idler pulleys, water pump, aux belt. 4-6 hour job.
repairOptions.longevity: Essential preventative maintenance. Do not skip - catastrophic failure is costly.

repairOptions.tier: Cylinder head rebuild (if belt has snapped)
repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Remove cylinder head, replace bent valves, new guides and seals, timing components.
repairOptions.longevity: Required if belt has snapped and valves have contacted pistons.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Supply & fit, rebuilt engine with new timing belt, water pump, 12-month warranty
repairOptions.longevity: Best if belt has snapped (catastrophic valve damage) or if head rebuild + other work exceeds 60% of replacement cost.

problems.vehicleValueCheck: For a Golf 1.2/1.4 TSI worth £4,000-£10,000, a timing belt service at specialist rates (£450-£750) is essential preventative maintenance. If the belt has snapped, weigh the £1,500-£2,500 head rebuild against a £1,600-£3,200 full rebuilt engine - the warranty and peace of mind on the full replacement often make it the better choice.
problems.recommendation: If you don't know when the timing belt was last changed on your Golf 1.2/1.4 TSI (EA211), get it done immediately. It's the single most important preventative measure on this engine. Combine it with the water pump and tensioner while everything is apart.
problems.cta: -> Compare rebuilt EA211 Volkswagen Golf TSI engine prices

problems.affectedModels: Volkswagen Golf 1.2 TSI and 1.4 TSI (all codes, 2005-2020)
problems.rootCause: Direct-injection engines suffer from carbon buildup on intake valves - there is no fuel wash to keep them clean. Turbocharger oil leaks and wastegate actuator failure are also common on higher-mileage units. Ignition coil failures are frequent on TSI engines.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Intake manifold removal, walnut shell blasting of intake valves to remove carbon deposits. 4-6 hour job.
repairOptions.longevity: Recommended every 60,000 miles as preventative maintenance on direct-injection turbo engines.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Remove and replace turbo, replace oil feed pipe, flush oil system, recalibrate.
repairOptions.longevity: Required if turbo has excessive play, oil seal failure, or actuator fault.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Supply & fit, rebuilt engine with refreshed turbo, new injectors, 12-month warranty
repairOptions.longevity: Best if multiple issues coexist (turbo + carbon + timing) and repair cost exceeds 60% of replacement cost.

problems.vehicleValueCheck: For a Golf TSI worth £3,000-£8,000, carbon cleaning (£350-£600) is excellent value - restoring lost performance for minimal outlay. A turbo replacement (£800-£1,500) is viable on cars worth over £4,000. If both need replacement, a full rebuilt engine with warranty becomes competitive.
problems.recommendation: Regular carbon cleaning at 60,000-mile intervals can restore lost performance. If your Golf TSI has lost boost or is making turbo noises, get it diagnosed immediately - a turbo replacement caught early is far cheaper than a full engine rebuild.
